questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The opportunities in the city and the academic courses

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Socially it's a 10, but the rigid administration at KU and the no-rules administration at Dauphine has made it hard

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I could not find the needed. So I had to just arrive and wish for the best and find the information myself being here.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nothing besides an international office at Dauphine where I could go and get help

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: You don't know when your courses starts, you don't know how to login to MyDauphine, You can't see the time schedule of the chosen courses as a student so you have no idea which courses to choose etc.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend finding housing through Dauphine although Dauphine and Crous should highen their corporation as they wanted to send me on the streets because the contract from Dauphine housing was not valid. Agree upon which contract is valid and make sure that the students that gets a room through Dauphine actually gets a room

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I can't liv on campus so c'est la vie

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing itself is super, but I think it's in the contract of the people working here that they have to hate young students because they are very evil to us

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It's 1 guy that fix it all for everyone: Nidhal. Big help, but please make it online so that the students are less frustrated and Nidhal does not have to work the whole day the first month

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: same as last comment

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: same as last comment

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. I got half of the ones I wanted as they don't have so many master courses for exchange students and the times schedules does not match

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to Nidhal at the international office at Dauphinewhen you arrive and decide your final courses, but be aware that he does not know your skills

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Liberty is good, but as Dauphine expects a lot from the students, please expect some things from the teachers as well. For example keeping deadlines, making sure they don't give us 3 presentations to make in 24 hours etc. Some rules for the teachers would be good

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Content and presentation skills where high, but academic writing very low. Some teachers expect you to use a lot of time on some things that does not make a lot of sense instead of using the time in a logic way. But I most say; it's SO good with all the teacher that is working when they are not teaching at Dauphine, they are often realistic.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Way more practical, much better for me than a CPH. Although the academic writing skills does not get trained as much as at CPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Supermarkets are expensive but the rent here is cheap when it's through Crous

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: A lot of sports for 70 euros for the whole semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the sports at Dauphine

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: See some more of France, there is a lot of opportunities. Otherwise Paris has sooo many cozy areas

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Hmm the language barrier can be hard if you don't speak french, so learn some before

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Choose courses with the French students instead of only international courses and eat lunch with them to get a relation

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The administration system is soooo slow and French people can be very negative especially if you speak english

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The french humor. they have a good humor and the students at Dauphine often want to make international friends, you just have to do something to involve with them

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1) Use Dauphine housing service to live cheap and get international friends, 2) Don't stress about the courses, you can change them at the international office when you arrive, 3) Make sure that you can login to MyDauphine before arriving

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have patience! And push if something is important. French people like to relax

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: You get so close with the culture and get a lot of good international friends that later become connections

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The communication with Crous, where I live, to make sure that I had my room. I had to push them for hours on my arrival ti make them find a room for me even though I had a contract etc. with Dauphine Housing Service

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
